task.description:
WF-03 Step 3 for ISS-0911. Implement lib/letflow/design/iss0911-start-instance-dialog-exact-lookup.md's PASSed design in full: (1) add useActiveDefinitionByName(name) hook to web/src/hooks/useDefinitions.ts calling definitionsApi.getActive, keyed via the existing definitionKeys.active(name) factory in web/src/api/useTenantScopedQueryKeys.ts. (2) In InstanceBoardPage.tsx's onStartDefinitionNameChange, replace the definitionTypeahead.items scan with a debounced call into the new hook keyed on the dialog's own startDefinitionName (use the existing useDebounce hook, 300ms, matching DefinitionListPage.tsx's convention per the design). (3) Implement the 5-state version-field model (idle/loading/found/not_found/error) via a deriveVersionLookupState()-shaped function, wiring the version display input's value/placeholder per each state. (4) Leave definitionTypeahead's other two call sites (onResolveDefinition at the page-level onBlur, and the datalist suggestions) untouched.

Run web/'s standard gates: `npm run type-check && npm run lint && npm test && npm run guards`, quoting real output. If web/tests/e2e/pipelines/platform-definition-promotion-rollback.pipeline.e2e.spec.ts exists and can plausibly be exercised via any available local harness, note whether you attempted it -- but this environment likely has no live backend, so state explicitly if a live e2e run is not possible rather than claiming one.
acceptance_criteria: the fix calls definitionsApi.getActive(name) (or an equivalent exact-match backend lookup) keyed on the dialog's own typed value, not the page-level filtered list
a race-guard against out-of-order async responses (rapid typing) is genuinely in place, matching the PASSed design's TanStack Query per-key cache isolation approach
the version field's loading/not-found/found states are all implemented with no gap
definitionTypeahead's other two call sites are unchanged
web/'s type-check, lint, test, and guards gates all pass, real output quoted

result.summary: Implemented the PASSed design in full. Added useActiveDefinitionByName(name) to web/src/hooks/useDefinitions.ts: queryKey definitionKeys.active(trimmedName), queryFn definitionsApi.getActive(trimmedName), enabled: trimmedName.length > 0, retry() returns false on error.status === 404 (so a 404 'no active definition yet' is not retried), staleTime left at the query client's global default (main.tsx) rather than an inline literal, per the design's explicitly sanctioned alternative and to avoid tripping the 'inline-stale-time' source guard (CAC-UI-01), which only exempts web/src/api/queryKeys.ts and web/src/main.tsx -- no allowedPaths exemption was added. InstanceBoardPage.tsx: onStartDefinitionNameChange no longer scans definitionTypeahead.items -- it only calls setStartDefinitionName(value). A new debouncedStartDefinitionName = useDebounce(startDefinitionName, 300) feeds useActiveDefinitionByName; a co-located deriveVersionLookupState() derives idle/loading/found/not_found/error from that query's isFetching/isSuccess/isError/error/data. A new useEffect reacts to found (sets startDefinitionVersion+startDefinitionId together, pushes definitionName/definitionId into searchParams -- preserving the ISS-0891 atomic-set invariant) and not_found/error (clears both); idle/loading leave current values untouched to avoid a flicker-to-empty mid-edit. The version input's value stays bound to startDefinitionVersion; its placeholder layers the new lookup states (loading/not_found/error messages) under the pre-existing page-level isLoadingActiveDefinition case. onResolveDefinition (page-level onBlur) and the <datalist> suggestions -- the other two definitionTypeahead call sites -- are byte-for-byte unchanged. Updated InstanceBoardPage.tenant-isolation.test.tsx's useDefinitions mock to add the new export (it was the only existing test importing InstanceBoardPage.tsx through that mock; it failed before the fix with 'No useActiveDefinitionByName export is defined on the mock'). Gates, run from web/: `npm run type-check` -- clean (tsc -b, no errors). `npm run lint` -- clean (eslint, --max-warnings 0, no output). `npm test` -- 141 test files passed, 958 tests passed, 0 failed. `npm run guards` -- 52 guard tests passed (source-scan, bundle-scan, meta-control, role-set), 0 violations; the build step inside guards succeeded. web/tests/e2e/pipelines/platform-definition-promotion-rollback.pipeline.e2e.spec.ts exists but was NOT run: curl against http://localhost:4000 returned no connection (exit 7, no listener) -- there is no live Letflow backend reachable in this environment, so a live Playwright e2e run against real data is not possible here; this is stated explicitly rather than claimed. No shim, no forbidden storage mechanism, no guard weakening -- the one guard hit (inline-stale-time on a literal `staleTime: 0`) was resolved by removing the inline value and relying on the existing global QueryClient default, not by exempting the file.
result.next_action: Route to SECURITY-REVIEWER then REVIEWER. Recommendation: SECURITY-REVIEWER should be free to judge this out of scope on its own review, but is not pre-judged here -- this change does not touch tenant resolution (tenantKeys.definitions.active is the existing tenant-scoped key factory, unmodified), auth/token handling, or response shaping (definitionsApi.getActive/ProcessDefinition shape are pre-existing and untouched); it only adds a new call site for an existing, already-used endpoint and changes client-side UI state derivation. Given core-directives' rule that frontend changes touching tenant resolution/token handling/response shaping need SECURITY-REVIEWER 'exactly as backend ones do', and none of those three apply here, SECURITY-REVIEWER can likely fast-pass this, but that determination is SECURITY-REVIEWER's to make, not FRONTEND-DEV's to skip.
